clues: This city sits in northern Iran, between the Caspian Sea coast and the mountains. It is the largest city on that whole coast.
Rain falls a lot here because the city sits between the sea and the mountains. Just south is a green rain forest, while most of Iran is dry.
Its past goes back to the 1200s. Much later, in Safavid times, it was a main hub for silk, with many cloth workshops.
Traders once called this place the Gate of Europe. Its roads and trade linked Iran with Russia and the rest of Europe.
In 2015 the world named this a top food city. UNESCO put it on its list of creative cities for its cooking.
